title: Redemption is rate-limited after the fact because the amount received is unknowable in advance
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.2.3.1 flags the deviation explicitly: "Unlike deposits and withdrawals, this operation applies its rate limit **after** redemption rather than before, since the resulting assets are not known until the shares are redeemed." A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.2.3.3 then decrements `LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW` "by the actual `assets` received, after the redemption is executed."

The cause is a real asymmetry in the ERC-4626 interface. `withdraw` is denominated in assets, so the amount to charge against the limit is known up front. `redeem` is denominated in shares, and the assets those shares fetch depend on the vault's state at execution. There is no way to charge the correct amount beforehand without trusting a preview call, which is exactly the quantity an adversarial vault could misreport.

Charging **realized** assets is therefore the more conservative choice: the limit is consumed by what actually left the vault, not by an estimate. Enforcement still holds because the decrement reverts when the remaining allowance is insufficient, and the revert unwinds the redemption in the same transaction.

Two further details matter. Redemption and withdrawal **share one allowance** (`LIMIT_4626_WITHDRAW`), so the two exit routes cannot be used in parallel to double the effective exit rate — the limit governs value leaving the position regardless of which function moved it. And because the whitelist is the rate limit (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.2.1.2), redemption inherits the same permissioning as withdrawal with no separate configuration.

The generalizable rule: when a call's magnitude is only knowable from its result, check after and rely on atomic revert rather than trusting a pre-flight estimate.
description: redeemERC4626 executes first and then decrements the shared withdraw allowance by the actual assets received, so the limit is consumed by realized value rather than by a requested amount.
